title: WinRM host spawns a suspicious child process
description: Detects wsmprovhost.exe spawning a command interpreter or administrative utility associated with remote execution.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use Windows Remote Management to execute discovery, transfer or command activity on a remote Windows endpoint.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents WinRM remote services and recommends correlating remote sessions with child-process creation, while SigmaHQ maintains a high-severity wsmprovhost child-process analytic; approved administration uses the same service.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected command, transfer and discovery utilities spawned directly by wsmprovhost while leaving its normal hosting children, other parents, caller-side WinRS activity and missing parent context unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Identify the remote-management source, initiating identity and child command, then validate the session against approved administration.
steps: Review the complete child command, account, target device, process tree and the surrounding WinRM session evidence.
Correlate network connections, remote logons, file creation, service or scheduled-task changes and follow-on processes on the target.
Confirm an approved automation, support or administration change; isolate the target and investigate the source identity when unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved PowerShell remoting, configuration management, support and administrative automation through WinRM

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected children spawned by wsmprovhost; do not match normal children, another parent, caller-side WinRS activity or missing parent context.
